title: Q1. Left Rotate an Array by One Position
statement:
Given an array of n integers, move the first element to the end and shift every other element one position to the left. Print the resulting array.

Input format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers

Output format:
Print the rotated array with spaces between elements.

Example:
Input:
5
1 2 3 4 5
Output:
2 3 4 5 1

title: Q2. Common Elements of Two Arrays (No Duplicates)
statement:
Given two arrays, print the distinct elements that occur in both arrays. Each common value must be printed only once, even if it appears multiple times in either input array. Print the values in the order in which they first appear in the first array.

Input format:
Line 1: n m
Line 2: n integers for the first array
Line 3: m integers for the second array

Output format:
Print the common distinct elements separated by spaces. If there are no common elements, print -1.

Example:
Input:
6 5
4 9 4 2 7 9
8 4 4 9 1
Output:
4 9

title: Q3. Find the Leaders in an Array
statement:
An element is a leader if it is strictly greater than every element to its right. The last element is always a leader. Given an array, print all leaders from left to right.

Input format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers

Output format:
Print the leaders in their original left-to-right order.

Example:
Input:
6
16 17 4 3 5 2
Output:
17 5 2

title: Q4. Difference Between the Second Maximum and Second Minimum
statement:
Given an array containing at least two distinct values, find the second smallest distinct element and the second largest distinct element. Print: second largest - second smallest. Duplicates do not create new ranks.

Input format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers

Output format:
Print one integer.

Example:
Input:
6
7 2 9 4 9 1
Output:
5

The second smallest is 2 and the second largest is 7, so 7 - 2 = 5.

title: Q5. Left Rotate an Array by K Positions
statement:
Given an array of n integers and an integer k, rotate the array to the left by k positions. Rotations wrap around, and k may be greater than n.

Input format:
Line 1: n k
Line 2: n space-separated integers

Output format:
Print the rotated array with spaces between elements.

Example:
Input:
7 3
1 2 3 4 5 6 7
Output:
4 5 6 7 1 2 3

title: Q6. Maximum Sum Mountain Subarray
statement:
A mountain subarray is a contiguous subarray with a strictly increasing part followed immediately by a strictly decreasing part. It must contain at least three elements and have a peak: a[i-1] < a[i] > a[i+1]. Equal adjacent values break a mountain. Find the maximum sum among all mountain subarrays. If the array contains no mountain, print 0.

Input format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers

Output format:
Print the maximum mountain sum.

Example:
Input:
8
1 3 5 4 2 6 7 1
Output:
15

The mountain [1, 3, 5, 4, 2] has sum 15.

title: Q7. Maximum Length of a Mountain
statement:
A mountain is a contiguous sequence that strictly increases for one or more steps, then strictly decreases for one or more steps. A peak is required, so a purely increasing or purely decreasing sequence is not a mountain. Equal adjacent values break a mountain. Find the length of the longest mountain. If no mountain exists, print 0.

Input format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers

Output format:
Print one integer: the length of the longest mountain.

Example:
Input:
9
2 3 5 4 2 1 6 7 5
Output:
6

The longest mountain is [2, 3, 5, 4, 2, 1].

title: Q8. Gas Station Circuit
statement:
There are n gas stations on a circular route. gas[i] is the gas available at station i, and cost[i] is the gas needed to travel from station i to station (i + 1) modulo n. Start with an empty tank at one station and travel clockwise around the circuit exactly once. Find the starting station index if a complete trip is possible; otherwise print -1. If a solution exists, it is unique. Station indices are zero-based.

Input format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers for gas
Line 3: n integers for cost

Output format:
Print the starting index, or -1.

Example:
Input:
5
1 2 3 4 5
3 4 5 1 2
Output:
3
